Other Christians accept the mechanisms of evolution while believing that God creates through these processes. For them, mechanism and Creator do not conflict.

blocks.h: How far the metaphor goes
The new life the Bible describes is far more thorough than “a bit better”: the old is buried, and the new rises.
We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.
The self-centered life must fall to the ground and die, and Christ Himself walked this road first.

I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
How far the metaphor does not go

A butterfly does not depend on grace; its genes carry it through on schedule. A person’s new birth cannot start itself. When Nicodemus asked how a man can be born again when he is old, Jesus answered with the Spirit. Also, a butterfly emerges all at once, while the Christian’s renewal is a lifelong lesson.
not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings, and have put on the new man, who is being renewed in knowledge after the image of his Creator,

Find a photo of yourself from many years ago. Look at the face then, and think about what God has changed in you over the years, and what is still the same you. Say one thing you are thankful for to God.
Meditate: Which old habit in me have I been trying to “improve” on my own? What if what it needs is to be crucified, not improved?

Pray: Lord who makes people new, thank You that Your grace is not a bit of encouragement for me but new life. Thank You, Lord Jesus, that You died for me and rose again. You who began a good work in me, I ask You to complete it. Holy Spirit, keep renewing my mind, so that it is no longer I who live. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: From self-centered to selfless: First admit that the old self needs to die, not merely to be given more training. Ask once a day: in this matter, am I reigning, or is Jesus reigning?
Change your mindset → change your life → change your lifestyle: Renewal begins in the mind (Romans 12:2). Pick one idea you picked up from the world and re-examine it with the Bible.
The Holy Spirit is my guide: A butterfly does not have to strive, but we must cooperate. Yet do not compare your progress with others; His timetable is different in each person.

blocks.h: This week: Write down one thing that God has truly changed in you since you came to faith, or over these past few years, and tell one person. If there is none, you can also honestly ask God to begin.
Pass it on: Do you think a person can really change completely? Have you ever seen it?
Small quiz

quiz.q: What mainly builds the adult structures during the pupal stage?
o: A perfectly uniform pot of soup
quiz.e: Imaginal discs are cell clusters set aside since the embryo stage, and they grow into wings, legs and other structures when the time comes.

quiz.q: What did Blackiston’s 2008 experiment find?
o: All memories from the larval period are kept
Fifth-instar trained larvae still avoided the odor after growing into moths
Butterflies do not need to go through a pupal stage
quiz.e: Larvae trained at the third instar did not retain it. The authors also note that this is consistent with the survival of neural connections but is not conclusive.

quiz.q: What is the greatest limit of the caterpillar-to-butterfly metaphor for new birth?
o: A butterfly is a natural process, while new life comes from God’s grace
quiz.e: A metaphor helps understanding, but a person’s new birth does not run on a program and does not come from ourselves.

questions.q: Is life a chemical accident, or does it come from a Lord who gives life?
Am I willing to be like a grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies, so that my life bears much fruit?
Can I accept evolution and still believe in God?
